key_insight: Inequality constraints can be incorporated directly into Gaussian process PDE solvers as a valid sequential conditioning step, turning admissibility requirements like positivity, monotonicity, and no-arbitrage into part of the probabilistic update.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to enforce physically or economically meaningful constraints in scientific computing without changing the underlying PDE solver pipeline.
method: Condition a GP prior on PDE residuals, boundary data, and measurements to form a physics-informed posterior.
Treat finite-dimensional inequality constraints as a second conditioning step via truncated-Gaussian moments.
Use the equality-conditioned posterior as the prior for virtual inequality observations.
evidence_signal: Across Poisson reconstruction, option pricing, and air-quality experiments, the constrained approach improved errors and constraint satisfaction, including a 63% error reduction on Poisson, 22% lower extrapolation error on thin S&P 500 option data, and a 74% reduction in sub-zero-tail proxy for air-quality fields.
watch_item: The inequality update is computationally non-Gaussian and depends on virtual-point choices and truncated-moment calculations, which may affect scalability and numerical stability.
paper_title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
